question: Which fundamental law of chemistry is illustrated by the fact that hydrogen and oxygen always combine in a fixed 1 : 8 mass ratio to form water?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Law of Constant Proportions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Law of Constant Proportions**, also known as the **Law of Definite Proportions**, was proposed by **Joseph Proust** in the year **1799**.
 
• According to this law, a chemical compound always contains the same elements in the same proportion by mass, regardless of its source or the method of preparation.
 
• In the case of water, it is always composed of hydrogen and oxygen in a fixed **mass ratio of 1:8**. This means that for every 1 gram of hydrogen, there are 8 grams of oxygen in water.
 
• This law is universally applicable for pure chemical substances. For example, the ratio of sodium to chlorine in sodium chloride (NaCl) is always constant.
 
• In the given question, the fixed mass ratio of hydrogen and oxygen in water (1:8) is a direct illustration of the **Law of Constant Proportions**.
